text.p: Computer manufacturer Tulip said on Thursday it was planning to buy unlisted sector rival Commodore BV in Nieuw-Vennep, the Netherlands.
Tulip said it would issue new shares to finance the takeover and added the acquisition was expected to have a clear positive impact on earnings per share from 1998.
Tulip reiterated it expected a profit for the whole of 1997.
In March Tulip announced a net loss of 10.0 million guilders for the whole of 1996.
Tulip said its turnover was expected to increase to some one billion guilders in 1998 as result of the takeover.
In 1996 Tulip reported turnover of 528 million guilders.
Tulip said it expected synergy-advantages from the takeover.
The current shareholders of Commodore, Halder Investments and Alpinvest, have granted a subordinated loan to Tulip as part of the takeover deal.

"As result of this they will gain the right to acquire 450,000 new Tulip Computers shares at a price of 20 guilders per share over a period of five years," it said. Tulip said it was mulling an issue of up to 30 million guilders.
Tulip said it would gain a market share of 8 to 10 percent in the netherlands after the takeover was completed.
Commodore sales amounted to 152 million guilders in 1996.
Commodore sells its computers in over 11 European countries.
